summary: Gottlieb Siegfried Bayer was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg and under Christoph Theodosius Walther. He held posts in Königsberg and became a professor at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences in 1726.

Gottlieb Wilhelm Leitner was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He studied at King's College London, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. He taught at King's College, led Government College Lahore and Oriental College, and helped found Punjab University and Woking's Oriental Institute.

Gouriswar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Alfred Bloch from around 1964 to 1967 and served as a Lehrbeauftragter at the Free University of Berlin from circa 1974 to 1989.

Govind Chandra Pande was an Indian historian, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor and vice-chancellor at the universities of Allahabad and Rajasthan, and chaired the Allahabad Museum and the IIAS.

Govind Kumar Meena is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Mahatma Gandhi Antarrashtriya Hindi Vishwavidyalaya and Banaras Hindu University before becoming an assistant professor at Government College University, Lahore in 2022.

Govind Sadashiv Ghurye was an Indologist and sociologist. He studied at Bahauddin College, Elphinstone College, and Cambridge under W. H. R. Rivers and Alfred Cort Haddon. He headed the sociology department at the University of Mumbai from 1924 to 1959.

Govind Swamirao Gai was an Indologist, epigraphist, and historian. He served as Chief Epigraphist for the Government of India and the Archaeological Survey of India (1966–1976), and later as an epigraphy consultant for the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Govind Vinayak Devasthali was an Indology scholar who studied under Hari Damodar Velankar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at HPT Arts & RYK Science College (attested 1944) and as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1968).

Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt was an Indologist who served as a professor at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (attested 1933–1939) and later succeeded Benoytosh Bhattacharyya as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1953–1957).
Grace Constant Lounsbery was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bryn Mawr College from circa 1895 to 1899. In 1929, she founded Les Amis du Bouddhisme, serving as its president until 1964.

Grace Morley was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist educated at UC Berkeley and the University of Paris. She directed the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art and the National Museum, New Delhi, and headed the International Council of Museums (1967–1978).

Grace S. Fong is a sinologist who studied at McGill University and the University of British Columbia. She taught as a professor at Smith College (~1985–1989) and served as associate professor and East Asian Studies department chair at McGill (~1993).

Grace Sturtevant Hopkins was a linguist who earned her undergraduate degree at Vassar College (~1920–1924) and her Ph.D. at Yale University (~1928–1932), where she studied under Edgar Howard Sturtevant.

Graeme MacQueen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi from circa 1972 to 1979 and served as a lecturer at McMaster University from circa 1977 to 2013.

Grafton Elliot Smith was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Sydney, Sydney Medical School, and St John's College, Cambridge, and later held a post at University College London from circa 1919 to 1936.
Graham E. Clarke was a Tibetologist who held posts at the Institute of Development Studies and was attested in 1998 as a Senior Member at the University of Oxford.
Graham Lock is a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied under Hsuan Hua and Saddhaloka Bhikkhu.

Graham Parkes is a scholar of philosophy and Japanese studies. After completing his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley, he taught at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1979–2008) and University College Cork (2008–2016), later becoming a research fellow at Vienna.

Graham Priest is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge and the LSE under John Lane Bell, later holding professorships at the University of Melbourne and the City University of New York Graduate Center.
Graham Sandberg was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at Trinity College Dublin and the Inner Temple, and later served as a chaplain for the Government of India from 1885 to 1904.
